name: Sunehusk
description: Hold the haft across the body with the blade tip raised so the curve covers the lead shoulder.

name: Short Habakiring
description: Swing the curved edge in a flat arc at waist height from the rear side to the lead side.

name: Quick Mawashi
description: Slide the rear hand along the shaft and drive the blade point straight at the throat.

name: Leaden Tsubaring
description: Lift the blade from beside the hip in an upward diagonal arc to cut under the arm.

name: Resting Nagaheel
description: Press the middle of the shaft against an incoming weapon and push it outward from the body.

name: Nagihop
description: Slide the rear foot forward along the ground while the blade stays level so the distance closes.

name: Raised Ishizukibase
description: Place the hands a forearm apart on the shaft and square the shoulders so the haft blocks the centre line.

name: Sunebump
description: Bring the edge down from the high rear side across the body toward the opposite hip.

name: Gnawing Bladecurve
description: Drop the blade low and sweep the curve at shin height to cut the front leg.

name: Forward Sayacap
description: When a foe closes inside the blade drive the butt cap of the shaft into the ribs.

name: Settled Ishizuki
description: Turn the shaft outward at the lead hand to knock a thrust past the hip.

name: Skipping Nagi
description: Swing the rear foot a quarter turn behind the lead foot so the blade faces a new line.

name: Angled Nagashaft
description: Shuffle backward in two short steps while holding the haft slanted across the chest.

name: Square Uchiotoshi
description: Flick the blade tip down onto the wrist of the foe's leading hand with a short snap.

name: Nagabump
description: Raise the shaft overhead and bring the edge down in a straight line onto the crown.

name: Planted Nagatip
description: Drop the blade point-down at the lead side so the haft stops a low cut aimed at the knee.

name: Ishiamble
description: Spring off the rear foot to carry the blade a full pace beyond the lead foot.

name: Stopping Harai
description: Slap the shaft across the foe's weapon arm so the guard is knocked off its line.

name: Ishizuki Stay
description: Stand with the blade raised beside the ear and the shaft slanting forward to cover the face.

name: Firm Kake
description: Pull the shaft from the lead hip outward in a wide arc so the edge crosses the foe's flank.

name: Ishistrike
description: Push the point forward along the centre line at the height of the throat with both arms extending.

name: Raised Nagatip
description: After any cut pull the blade back across the body into guard before the foe can answer.

name: Kake Drop
description: Angle the sweep downward so the curve bites the outer thigh of the lead leg.

name: Nagastay
description: Roll the shaft inward over an attacking weapon so the thrust slides toward the off side.

name: Locking Bladecurve
description: Hook the back of the blade over the foe's shaft and pull it down to unbalance the grip.

name: Backward Sukui
description: Step off the line of attack at an angle and plant the lead foot beside the foe's flank.

name: Hooding Nagablade
description: Grip the shaft at its balance point so the weapon floats level and can swing either end.

name: Hard Habakiring
description: Shift the whole body weight onto the lead foot as the edge falls on a slanting line.

name: Sukuidrop
description: Let the blade swing back across the body on the return and cut a second time on the same arc.

name: Nagablade Lid
description: Lift the shaft with both hands over the head so a downward blow lands on the wood.

name: Swaying Nagashaft
description: Slide the rear hand to the butt and step away so the blade holds the foe at its tip.

name: Kind Tsubaring
description: Rest the flat of the blade lightly on the foe's weapon to feel the pressure and read the next movement.

name: Lowered Ishizukibase
description: Choke up on the shaft near the blade heel so the weapon can turn tightly inside the foe's reach.

name: Sudden Sayacap
description: Chop with the thick base of the edge near the shaft when the foe stands too close for the tip.

name: Short Nagi
description: Whip the shaft end around and drive the butt cap into the soft part of the stomach.

name: Sukuistay
description: Hook the shaft behind the foe's ankle and pull to take the foot off the ground.

name: Resting Nagatip
description: Spin the butt end up to meet a low cut and turn it away from the leg.

name: Swaying Uchiotoshi
description: Turn on the ball of the lead foot to put the shaft between the body and a closing foe.

name: Level Sukui
description: From the choked grip jab the blade point short and quick at the hollow of the throat.

name: Hooding Nagashaft
description: Let a thin thread of qi settle in the hands so the grip stays firm while the shaft is guarded.

name: Nagi Blow
description: Release the breath at the start of the sweep so a little qi follows the edge across the arc.

name: Nagaheel Drop
description: Turn the hips sharply and cut along the foe's ribs with a light pulse of qi in the blade.

name: Nagacowl
description: Circle the shaft in a small ring so a weak thread of qi turns the incoming blow aside.

name: Shifting Harai
description: Skim forward in a low gliding step with qi lightening the rear foot.

name: Tending Ishizukibase
description: Hold the blade point near the foe's chest and feel the shifts of his stance through the shaft.

name: Folded Habakiring
description: Stand at the exact blade length from the foe so every sweep lands only with the tip.

name: Open Harai
description: Whip the farthest part of the curve through the foe's guard with a small qi pulse at the tip.

name: Haraidrop
description: Step in behind a straight thrust so the point reaches a foe who thought himself out of range.

name: Shifting Ishizuki
description: Glide back one blade length while the shaft stays pointed at the foe's lead knee.

name: Ishilid
description: Press the blade flat on the ground ahead of the foe's lead foot to stop the step.

name: Sayacap Lid
description: Roll the shaft between the palms in a steady spin so qi spreads along its length and covers the front.

name: Kakehit
description: Trace a figure eight in front of the body so the edge cuts on each loop of the path.

name: Haraihop
description: Pass the shaft between the hands and change the lead foot together so the weapon switches sides.

name: Lowered Bladecurve
description: Wheel the blade over the head in a full circle to sweep a falling cut off to either side.

name: Nagadash
description: Slide to the butt with one hand and fling the blade out at full extension across the foe's forearm.

name: Straight Uchiotoshi
description: Keep the shaft pressed against the foe's weapon and lean in so he cannot lift it for a swing.

name: Hitching Mawashi
description: Spin the shaft off a bind and slip the blade free before the foe can follow the contact.

name: Folded Nagablade
description: End a spin by planting the butt cap and settling the weight into a low firm guard.

name: Snug Nagaheel
description: Match each footfall to the shaft so the guard shifts as one piece with the body.

name: Sudden Sukui
description: Land the lead foot at the moment the edge arrives so the cut carries the full weight of the step.

name: Nimble Mawashi
description: Step wide of the foe's centre line and cut across the open side in the same breath.

name: Sunestrike
description: Scoop the curve upward under the foe's shin with a touch of qi to lift the cut.

name: Snug Tsubaring
description: Hold the shaft crosswise before the chest so qi in the wood stops a heavy downward chop.

name: Sukuipause
description: Tap the foe's blade at an offbeat to break the rhythm of his attack.

name: Uchiotoshi Dodge
description: Skip backward off the butt cap planted on the ground to pull out of a charge.

name: Planted Habakiring
description: Hold the blade out to one side with the shaft trailing so the open arc is ready to swing.

name: Ishidash
description: Turn the whole body and swing the edge in a full horizontal circle at chest height.

name: Ishihusk
description: End the wide swing by braking the shaft against the lead forearm so no opening shows.

name: Ishibump
description: Reverse the wide swing without a pause and cut back along the same line at the foe's opening.

name: Lowered Nagatip
description: Sweep the shaft broadly sideways to brush two incoming weapons wide of the body.

name: Haraiskitter
description: Circle the foe at blade length with short side steps so the long arc always has room.
